D021-D013_h001.question:
It's been about six months now, and I just feel… drained. I barely eat. I mean, I really watch what goes in my body—calorie counting has become an obsession. I can't even look at a piece of cake or anything with a lot of fat without feeling this intense panic that I'll just balloon up immediately. I've lost so much weight, and frankly, I just keep wanting to lose more. Every morning, I weigh myself, and if it hasn't gone down, I get so upset with myself; it completely wrecks my day.

On top of all this, I just feel so incredibly low. There’s a constant sadness hanging over me, and I have absolutely no energy for anything, even for the clients I used to care so much about. My boss has noticed, and my performance reviews have started to slip. I know I should feel something, but it's like a gray cloud has settled over everything. I know food restriction and weight loss is often accompanied by depressive symptoms, but the biggest problem is that I'm just so terrified of gaining weight. That's what really drives all of this.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
